questions.independent_solution: Let f(x)=ln x+1/x for x>0. A tangent with slope 2/9 touches at an abscissa s satisfying f′(s)=(s−1)/s²=2/9. This is equivalent to (2s−3)(s−3)=0, so the two tangencies occur at s=3/2 and s=3. The y-intercept is b(s)=f(s)−2s/9. Thus b(3/2)=ln(3/2)+1/3 and b(3)=ln 3−1/3. Since b′(s)=−(2s−3)(s−3)/(9s²)>0 for 3/2<s<3, b(3)>b(3/2), so the absolute difference is ln 2−2/3.

Then 1+√h=9(1−√h), so √h=4/5. This value is in the required range and yields the progression.

questions.independent_solution: With f(x)=e^x−1−x, the derivative e^x−1 makes f strictly decreasing on (−∞,0) and increasing on (0,∞). Its minimum is f(0)=0, and it tends to +∞ at both ends. Therefore f(x)=t for t>0 has exactly one root u<0 and one v>0. Put w=−u and F(s)=f(−s), which strictly increases for s>0. The function e^v−e^(−v)−2v vanishes at 0 and has positive derivative for v>0, so F(v)<f(v)=F(w), yielding v<w. Since v+t=e^v−1, F(v+t)−t=e^(1−e^v)−1+v. The latter expression vanishes at v=0 and has derivative 1−e^(1+v−e^v)>0 for v>0 because e^v>1+v. Hence F(v+t)>t=F(w) and w<v+t.
